_about.what: Elbow, wrist & hand — one move per object in "moves". The app reads this file directly: save it, reload the page. Every field name is checked, so a typo is reported with the file and move it is in.
_about.add: Copy a move that looks like the new one, paste it into "moves", give it a new id and change every field. Or: node scripts/catalog.js new <file> <id>  — writes a template with placeholder text to replace.
_about.remove: Delete the move's object (and the comma before or after it). Routines built in the app that used it will show it as missing.
_about.check: node scripts/catalog.js check  — or reload the app: a bad file shows the error on screen instead of the exercise list.
_about.names: Anything written as a word instead of an object — "metric": "knee", "template": "lean", "preset": "standing", "conditions": "balance" — is looked up in shared.json. Add reusable pieces there, not here.
_about.notes: Any field starting with "_" is a note for people and is ignored: "_note": "physio wants this re-checked".

fields.id: Unique name, used in links and saved sessions — never change it once the move has been used. Lower-case letters, digits, underscores. Good: "seated_knee_ext". Bad: "Seated Knee Ext", "knee-ext", "1_knee".
fields.name: What the user sees in the list. Good: "Seated knee extension". Bad: a clinical term nobody outside physio uses ("Open-chain terminal extension").
fields.clinicalName: Optional. The term a physio would use, shown in the details panel under the name.
fields.type: "reps" (counted) or "hold" (seconds in position). A stretch held for 30 s is a hold; ten slow raises are reps.
fields.view: "side" or "front" — where the phone stands. Side-on for anything that bends forward/back (knees, hips, spine); front-on for anything that goes out to the side (leg raise to the side, arm raise to the side, knees caving in).
fields.tracking: What the camera can honestly do: "form" (counts AND judges — needs at least one fault with a measurement and a threshold), "reps" (counts only; faults are listed for the person to watch), "none" (nothing to measure — the guide is shown and the set is logged by hand). Bad: "form" on a move whose faults are all words; the file will not load.
fields.vetted: Optional, true/false. true = a physio has recorded and checked this move in the Studio; vetted moves list first.
fields.equipment: List of words: ["none"], ["chair"], ["band", "door anchor"]. Optional extras say so: "ankle weight (optional)".
fields.muscles: { "primary": [...], "secondary": [...] } — plain names ("quadriceps", "gluteus medius"). primary must have at least one.
fields.sided: Only for one-sided moves: { "limb": "leg" | "arm" | "side", "by": "camera" | "pick", "auto": true }. "camera" = the limb nearest the phone is the working one (side-on moves); "pick" = the person chooses (front-on moves); "auto": true = when no side was chosen, watch both and follow the one that moves. Leave the field out for two-sided moves.
fields.upperBody: true when the legs need not be in frame (seated desk moves, shoulder work). Default false.
fields.summary: One line for the list. Good: "Sitting, straighten one knee until the leg is level, hold, and lower." Bad: a paragraph.
fields.setup: Where the phone goes and how to start, in the user's words. Good: "Sit tall on a chair, side-on to the phone, working leg nearest…" Bad: "Standard set-up."
fields.brief: What the coach SAYS out loud as the set begins: the position and the movement in one or two short sentences, no camera talk (the person has already placed the phone). Keep it under about 35 words — it is spoken while they get into position. Good: "Lie on your back, working leg straight. Slide the heel toward your bottom as far as it will go, then slide it back out." Bad: "Stand 2.5 m from the camera at hip height" (set-up, not movement) or a paragraph. Leave it out and the coach says only the name and the target.
fields.why: Why this camera angle can measure this move. Shown to the user; keeps the author honest. Good: "Side-on the knee angle runs from 90° to straight." Bad: left empty.
fields.calibrationPose: Optional. The still position held for the first two seconds of every set, which the coach measures against. Good: "Sitting tall, knee bent to 90°, foot hanging."
fields.camera: { "height": "floor" | "knee" | "hip" | "chest" | "eye", "distance": "2 m", "posture": "standing" | "sitting" | "lying" | "prone" | "sidelying" | "kneeling", "tolerance": 25 }. Leave it out to use the file's default at the top. posture also decides how the stick figure is pinned in place, and how a crooked phone is levelled at calibration (a standing or sitting trunk is upright, a lying one is along the floor; kneeling makes no assumption). tolerance: degrees the person may turn away from the ideal view mid-set before the coach says to turn back; leave it out for the settings.json default. Good: 20–30. Bad: 5 (nobody stands that still) or 60 (the joint is hidden by then).
fields.targets: Optional list of rep counts / hold seconds the bubble cycles through, e.g. [6, 8, 10, 12]. Leave it out for the standard choices in settings.json.
fields.defaultTarget: The one of targets selected to begin with. Must be in the list. Leave it out with targets.
fields.progress: How far through a rep the person is. { "metric": <measurement>, "start": "calibrated" | number, "target": number | "opt:rom" }. "calibrated" = whatever the measurement reads in the start position; "startMin"/"startMax" clamp it (a knee that calibrates at 150° is treated as 160°). target = the reading at a full rep, or with "targetIsDelta": true a change from the start — "delta": -1 when the reading goes DOWN during the rep (a knee angle closing). Only for type "reps" with tracking "form" or "reps". Good: knee angle from calibrated to 172. Bad: start and target the same number.
fields.show: What the coach asks the person to demonstrate once, before the set, so the target is measured on their body instead of assumed: { "ask": "arms straight out to the sides, level with your shoulders, nothing in your hands" }. They hold that pose still for a moment, with the band or weight out of the way, and what it reads becomes progress.target for the set. Only for a counted move, and only worth it when the number in progress.target depends on the body or the angle — a raise to shoulder height, a hands-apart distance — or when the equipment hides the joints. progress.target is still required: it is the fallback, and the sanity check (a demonstration under 40% or over 250% of it is refused). Good: one short sentence naming the end position. Bad: "do the exercise".
fields.hold: For type "hold" with tracking on: { "conditions": [ { "metric": <measurement>, "rel": "abs" | "change", "min": n, "max": n } ] } — the hold counts while every condition is met. "change" = relative to the calibrated start. A condition may carry "when": [{ "option": "variant", "is": "bent" }] so it only applies for that option. A named set ("balance") comes from shared.json.
fields.display: Optional. What the live readout shows: { "label": "bend", "unit": "°", "from": "start" } shows the progress measurement as a change from the start ("abs" = the raw reading); for a hold, { "condition": 0, "label": "knee", "aim": "90°" } shows that hold condition. Without it the app shows the raw progress reading.
fields.enterCue: Optional, holds only: what the coach says when the person has been out of position for a few seconds. Good: "Slide down the wall until your knees are at ninety".
fields.faults: What goes wrong, in the order they matter. Each: { "id", "label", "cue" (spoken, ≤ 8 words, what TO do), "tip" (written, why it matters), "severity" 1–3 }. Add "metric", "op" ("<" or ">"), "threshold" and the camera watches for it; leave those out and it is listed for the person to watch. "minP" (0–1) = ignore until this far into the rep; "persist" ms before it is spoken, "cooldown" ms before the same cue may repeat (rules included, so one that is true every rep is not said every rep); "rel": "change" compares to the calibrated start. "when": a list of gates that must all hold for the fault to count — { "option": "variant", "is": "bent" }, { "metric": <measurement>, "op": "<", "threshold": 168 }, "inPosition" or "notInPosition". "phase": "moving" / "rest" (reps), "any" (a hold fault that must fire while the person is OUT of position; otherwise hold faults only watch the held position), or "start" — read once on the start position before the set, for a set-up error that is unfixable later (heels too far away, knee already bent, band already taut); a start check may not be a rule and may not use "rel": "change", since the start is what it is judging. "scale": { "metric": "progress", "times": 0.35 } makes the threshold grow with another reading. Rules instead of a measurement: "rule": "shallow" (rep did not reach the target), "fast" with "minMs", "return" with "threshold" (rep ended above this progress — did not come all the way back). Or "template": "lean" with a "threshold" to reuse one from shared.json. Good cue: "Sit tall". Bad cue: "You are leaning back again" (tells them what is wrong, not what to do).
fields.guide: { "surface": what to stand/lie on, "stop": when to stop, "cannotSee": what the person must check themselves, "regions": [ { "name": "Trunk", "points": [ { "t": "one form point", "tracked": true|false } ] } ] }. tracked: true only when a fault with a measurement actually checks that point — it is shown to the user as "camera watches".
fields.pose: The two-frame stick figure. { "A": start keyframe, "B": end keyframe, "work": { "thigh": 1, "glute": 0.5 } muscles to light up 0–1, "props": [ { "kind": "box" | "bar" | "disc" | "band", "at": "hip" } ], "wall": "behind" | "ahead", "anchor": joint(s) that stay put }. Side-view keyframe angles in degrees: torso (from vertical, + = leaning forward), thigh & shin (from hanging straight down, + = forward), foot (+ = toes up), uarm & farm (arms, + = forward), plus the far limb: thighF, shinF, footF, uarmF, farmF; face: "right" | "left". Front-view: legL, legR, shinL, shinR, armL, armR, foreL, foreR (+ = out to the side), lean, headTilt, squat 0–1. "preset": "standing" | "seated" | "supine" | "prone" | "quadruped" fills the usual values first. Check it on /figures.html.
fields.tempo: Free text. Good: "Up 2 s, hold 2 s, down 3 s."
fields.contraindications: When not to do it. Shown as "Do not do this if".
fields.sources: Optional list of { "name", "url" } added to the file's own sources.
fields.band: Optional. "none", "yellow", "red"… = offers the band-colour bubble with that default; true = offers it defaulting to none.
fields.minMs: Optional, reps only: the quickest a rep may take before "Too fast" fires (when the move lists no live fault of its own). Default in settings.json.
fields.options: Advanced: extra bubbles, e.g. a range target { "key": "rom", "label": "Range target", "values": [45, 60, 75, 90], "unit": "°", "default": 90 } referenced from progress.target as "opt:rom".
fields.figure: Advanced: point keyframes captured by the Studio instead of pose angles. Prefer pose.
fields.focus: Advanced: the landmark the live view highlights, e.g. "KNEE". Default: the last point of the progress measurement.
fields.group: Optional. The heading the move is listed under; default = the file's group at the top.
fields.region: Optional. The body region for filtering; default = the file's region.
fields.icon: Optional short label used where an icon is expected. Default "move".
fields.order: Optional. Position in the list; default = the file's order + position in this file.

sources.name: Tyler & Thomas — eccentric training with the FlexBar (Tyler twist)

moves.name: Eccentric wrist extension
moves.summary: Forearm on a table, palm down, lift the weight with the other hand and lower it slowly with the working wrist.
moves.setup: Sit with the forearm resting on a table, wrist over the edge, palm down, a light weight in the hand. Use the other hand to lift the wrist up, then lower it slowly on its own over three to five seconds.
moves.why: The wrist tilts a few centimetres at the edge of a table — below what the pose model resolves. Logged by hand.
moves.contraindications: Sharp pain at the outside of the elbow that lingers after the set.

faults.label: Not assisting back up
faults.tip: Only the lowering is loaded. Use the other hand to return the weight to the top.

faults.label: Dropping the wrist
faults.tip: The slow lowering is the whole point; the way up is assisted.

faults.label: Elbow lifting off the support
faults.tip: The forearm rests on the thigh or table throughout so only the wrist moves.

faults.label: Forearm lifting off the table
faults.cue: Lift it back with the other hand
faults.tip: Only the wrist moves; pin the forearm down.

guide.surface: A table with the wrist over the edge.

points.t: Lowers slowly from up to hanging.

moves.name: Wrist curl
moves.summary: Forearm on the thigh, palm up, curl the weight up with the wrist and lower.
moves.setup: Sit with the forearm on the thigh, wrist past the knee, palm up, light weight in the hand. Curl the wrist up, hold a second, lower slowly.
moves.why: The movement is a few centimetres of hand travel. Logged by hand.
moves.contraindications: Pain at the inside of the elbow (golfer's elbow) that grows during the set.

faults.label: Elbow lifting
faults.tip: If the elbow rises the biceps are helping; keep it pinned on the thigh.

faults.label: Weight too heavy
faults.tip: These are small muscles. Heavy weight recruits the shoulder and irritates the elbow.

faults.label: Rushing
faults.tip: Three seconds to lower.

faults.label: Short range
faults.tip: Let the weight roll to the fingertips at the bottom and curl all the way up.

guide.surface: A chair; forearm on the thigh.
guide.stop: Pain on the inside of the elbow.

moves.name: Forearm rotation (pronation / supination)
equipment: hammer or light dumbbell held at one end
moves.summary: Elbow at 90° by the side, turn the palm up and then down with a hammer in the hand.
moves.setup: Sit or stand with the elbow tucked and bent to 90°, holding a hammer near the head end. Turn the palm up until the hammer points sideways, then down the other way. Slow and controlled.
moves.why: The forearm rotates on its own axis; the wrist barely changes position. Logged by hand.
moves.progression: Hold the hammer lower on the handle.

faults.label: Elbow drifting away from the side
faults.cue: Keep the elbow at your side
faults.tip: Tuck a towel under the arm to keep the elbow still.

faults.label: Shoulder rotating
faults.tip: If the elbow swings in and out, the shoulder is turning instead.

faults.label: Bending the wrist
faults.tip: The rotation comes from the forearm bones, not from flicking the wrist.

faults.label: Half turns
faults.tip: Go to both ends of the turn; the stiffness usually lives at the very end.

points.t: Rotates fully palm up and palm down.

moves.name: Tyler twist (FlexBar)
moves.summary: Twist a rubber bar with the good hand, then let the sore side untwist it slowly.
moves.setup: Hold the bar vertically in the sore hand, wrist bent back. Grip the top with the other hand and twist it. Bring both arms straight out in front, then slowly let the sore wrist straighten so the bar untwists.
moves.why: The action is inside the hands. Logged by hand.
moves.regression: Softer bar or a rolled towel.
moves.contraindications: Pain that stays after the set, or a numb hand.

faults.label: Untwisting too fast
faults.tip: The slow untwist loads the tendon; fast is wasted.

faults.label: Expecting it to be painless
faults.tip: A mild ache during and shortly after is normal and part of how this works; sharp or lasting pain is not.

faults.label: Elbows bending
faults.tip: Keep both elbows straight so the wrist does the work.

faults.label: Gripping too tightly
faults.tip: A death grip fatigues the hand before the tendon is loaded.

guide.stop: Pain that lingers or a numb hand.

moves.name: Grip squeeze
moves.summary: Squeeze a soft ball as hard as is comfortable, hold, relax.
moves.setup: Hold a soft ball or putty in the palm. Squeeze, hold five seconds, relax fully.
moves.why: The fingers do all the work. Logged by hand.
moves.contraindications: Pain in the fingers or a recent hand fracture without clearance.

faults.label: Holding the breath
faults.tip: Breath-holding spikes blood pressure during a hard grip. Keep breathing out.

faults.label: Wrist bending on the squeeze
faults.tip: Keep the wrist neutral so the fingers do the work.

faults.label: Holding the breath
faults.tip: Count out loud.

faults.label: Curling the wrist
faults.tip: A neutral wrist puts the work in the hand rather than the forearm tendons.

moves.name: Tendon glides
moves.summary: Move the fingers through straight, hook, fist, tabletop and straight fist positions.
moves.setup: Hold the hand up, fingers straight. Curl into a hook (fingertips to the base of the fingers), then a full fist, then a tabletop (knuckles bent, fingers straight), then a straight fist. Return to straight each time.
moves.why: Finger positions are below what the pose model tracks. Logged by hand.
moves.progression: Add a light stretch at each position.
moves.contraindications: Sharp pain or catching in a finger.

faults.label: Forcing a stiff finger
faults.tip: Glides are about moving the tendons, not stretching. Force makes a stiff hand stiffer.

faults.label: Skipping positions
faults.tip: Each shape glides a different tendon; go through them all.

faults.label: Wrist bending
faults.tip: Keep the wrist neutral so the glide is in the fingers.

faults.label: Not holding each shape
faults.tip: The hold is what glides the tendon through its sheath.

points.t: Straight → hook → fist → tabletop → straight fist.

moves.name: Wrist flexor stretch
moves.summary: Arm straight out, palm up, pull the fingers gently back toward you.
moves.setup: Straighten the arm in front, palm up. With the other hand, draw the fingers back toward the body until the front of the forearm stretches. Hold.
moves.why: The stretch is at the hand. Logged by hand.

faults.label: Elbow bending
faults.tip: A bent elbow takes the stretch off the forearm.

faults.label: Pulling too hard
faults.tip: A stretch, not a pain.

faults.label: Bouncing the stretch
faults.tip: A steady hold lengthens the tissue; bouncing just provokes it.

faults.label: Fingers not included
faults.tip: Straightening the fingers as well reaches the whole flexor group.

points.t: Straight, palm up, fingers drawn back.

moves.name: Wrist extensor stretch
moves.summary: Arm straight out, palm down, press the back of the hand down and toward you.
moves.setup: Straighten the arm in front, palm down, fingers relaxed. With the other hand, press the back of the hand down and toward the body until the top of the forearm stretches. Hold.
moves.why: The stretch is at the hand. Logged by hand.

faults.label: Elbow bending
faults.tip: A bent elbow takes the stretch off the forearm.

faults.label: Shoulder rising
faults.tip: Keep the shoulder relaxed so the stretch stays in the forearm.

faults.label: Bouncing the stretch
faults.tip: Steady and gentle. This tendon is usually already irritable.

faults.label: Open hand
faults.tip: A gentle fist adds the finger extensors to the stretch.

points.t: Straight, palm down, hand pressed down.

moves.name: Overhead triceps stretch
moves.summary: One arm overhead, elbow bent so the hand drops behind the neck; the other hand draws the elbow across.
moves.setup: Face the phone. Reach the working arm up, bend the elbow so the hand drops behind the head, and use the other hand on the elbow to draw it gently toward the midline. Hold.
moves.brief: Reach the working arm up, bend the elbow so the hand drops behind the head, and use the other hand on the elbow to draw it gently toward the midline.
moves.why: Facing the phone the working upper arm is held near vertical, so the timer runs only while the elbow is up.
moves.progression: Lean gently to the opposite side.

faults.label: Head pushed forward
faults.tip: Letting the head drift forward turns a triceps stretch into neck strain.

faults.label: Leaning away
faults.tip: A side lean fakes the stretch; keep the trunk upright.

faults.label: Shoulder hiking
faults.tip: Let the shoulder drop while the elbow points up.

faults.label: Arching the ribs
faults.tip: When the shoulder runs out of range the ribs flare. Stop before that.

points.t: Elbow up and drawn toward the midline.

moves.name: Elbow bend and straighten
moves.summary: Standing or sitting, bend the elbow fully so the hand comes to the shoulder, then straighten it fully.
moves.setup: Sit or stand side-on to the phone at chest height, working arm nearest, upper arm hanging by the side. Bend the elbow until the hand reaches the shoulder, then straighten fully. Keep the upper arm still.
moves.brief: Sit or stand with the upper arm hanging by the side. Bend the elbow until the hand reaches the shoulder, then straighten fully.
moves.why: From the side the shoulder–elbow–wrist angle runs from straight to fully bent each rep, and the upper arm swinging forward to help shows as the shoulder–elbow line leaving vertical.
moves.dosage: 3 × 10, several times a day after injury.
moves.progression: A light weight; a pause at each end.
moves.regression: Support the upper arm on a table.
moves.contraindications: Sharp pain or locking in the joint.

faults.label: Upper arm swinging forward
faults.tip: Pin the elbow to the side; only the forearm moves.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Not straightening fully
faults.tip: Full straightening is the range that gets lost after injury; finish each rep.

faults.label: Swinging from the shoulder
faults.tip: Pin the upper arm to your side so the movement is all at the elbow.

faults.label: Stopping short of the ends
faults.tip: Range is lost at the very ends. Go gently to both, every rep.
